test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
A magnet, when moved near a coil, produces an induced current. Which of the following method(s) can be used to increase the magnitude of the induced current?

(i) Increasing the number of turns in the coil

(ii) Increasing the speed of the magnet

(iii) Increasing the resistivity of the wire of the coil
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (ii)**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to** Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction**, the magnitude of the induced electromotive force (emf) in a coil is directly proportional to the rate of change of the magnetic flux through the coil.
 
• This can be expressed as: **Emf = -N (dΦ/dt)**, where N is the number of turns in the coil, and dΦ/dt is the rate of change of magnetic flux.
 
• Thus,** increasing the number of turns in the coil (statement (i)) will directly increase the magnitude of the induced emf, and hence the induced current, assuming the resistance of the coil remains constant**.
 
• **Increasing the speed of the magnet (statement (ii)) will increase the rate of change of magnetic flux (dΦ/dt), which will also increase the magnitude of the induced emf and the induced current.**
 
• However,** increasing the resistivity of the wire of the coil (statement (iii)) will increase the resistance of the coil, which according to Ohm's Law (V = IR) will decrease the current for a given emf. **Therefore, this method will not increase the magnitude of the induced current.
 
• Hence, the correct methods to increase the magnitude of the induced current are both (i) and (ii).
